grades.reason: Covers menvcfg FIOM and PBMTE bits and the data/I-O FENCE instruction. It says nothing about FENCE.I or instruction-fetch synchronization after writing code.

grades.quote: the behavior of FENCE.I is described in Chapter 5
grades.reason: Only says RVWMO does not formally describe FENCE.I and points to Chapter 5 for its behavior. It gives no rule for when FENCE.I is required.

grades.quote: it remains the only standard instruction-fetch coherence mechanism
grades.reason: A preface changelog. It notes that FENCE.I moved to Zifencei and is the only standard instruction-fetch coherence mechanism. That is useful background but does not say when it is required.

grades.quote: Memory writes to the jump vector table require an instruction barrier ( _fence.i_ ) to guarantee that they are visible to the instruction fetch.
grades.reason: Gives one concrete case where fence.i is required. Memory writes to the jump vector table must be followed by fence.i before they are visible to instruction fetch. It also says JVT can be switched without a barrier if the tables are unchanged since the last fence.i. It does not give the general rule for modified code.
